student: Frozen routed-v6 next-active-player spatial encoder plus 17 root-conditioned features; shared two-hidden-layer 128-ReLU scalar scorer trained for 20 epochs on robust SmoothL1 differences of asinh(native_reply_score/1000) against static rank zero, naturally map-balanced
decision: Reject. No full-game gate, rating, or deployment attempted; seed6300000 remains untouched.
interpretation: The transformed score regression generalized moderately in average error and achieved high pair-sign accuracy, but positive alternatives were rare: 1637/17731 validation pairs. Its predicted-positive precision was only 645/2076, so whole-slate selection incurred more native reply-score losses than gains versus static rank zero. This resolves the apparent contradiction between 14946/16987 sign accuracy and harmful decisions: the common negative class dominated the metric. Do not retune this model on seed6312000; the next attempt needs a controlled way to prioritize rare tactical gains or model the opponent response itself.
